sentences.en: When most of us think of a negotiation,

sentences.zh: 我们问自己他们在想什么

sentences.zh: 马克斯，你写过一位非常有前途的棒球运动员的职业生涯

sentences.zh: 名叫马修·哈灵顿。

sentences.zh: 在2000年，他曾登上《今日美国》和《美国棒球》杂志的专题报道。

sentences.en: How did those articles describe him?
sentences.zh: 那些文章是如何描述他的？

sentences.en: As a pleasant, earnest, future pitching superstar bound for the major leagues.
sentences.zh: 一个讨人喜欢、认真、注定要进入美国职业棒球大联盟的未来投手巨星。

sentences.en: So, he entered the draft in the year 2000 and he signed up with a major agent named
sentences.zh: 所以，他在2000年参加了选秀，并与一位名叫汤米·坦泽的大经纪人签约。

sentences.en: Tommy Tanzer.
sentences.zh: 汤米·坦泽。

sentences.en: What were the discussions before the draft happened in terms of how he was going to perform
sentences.zh: 在选秀发生之前，关于他将如何表现

sentences.en: and what kind of income he could expect to receive once the draft was done, Max?
sentences.zh: 以及选秀结束后他能期望获得什么样的收入，双方进行了怎样的讨论，马克斯？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, basically, the agent convinces young Mr. Harrington and his parents
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，这位经纪人说服年轻的哈灵顿先生和他的父母

sentences.en: that he's worth a very large amount of money.
sentences.zh: 他非常值钱。

sentences.en: They agree to put a price tag at a very high number
sentences.zh: 他们同意设定一个非常高的价格标签

sentences.en: that they're assuming that the baseball team will eventually cave in.
sentences.zh: 他们假设棒球队最终会妥协。

sentences.en: And, unfortunately, they don't.
sentences.zh: 而不幸的是，他们没有妥协。

sentences.en: And Tanzer basically encourages Harrington to be patient and wait for them to cave.
sentences.zh: 坦泽基本上鼓励哈灵顿保持耐心，等待他们妥协。

sentences.en: And under the rules of the major league baseball system,
sentences.zh: 根据美国职棒大联盟系统的规则，

sentences.zh: 潜在的雇员在任何特定年份只能与一支球队谈判。

sentences.en: And, basically, Tanzer and Harrington push the team to the limit
sentences.zh: 基本上，坦泽和哈灵顿把这支球队逼到了极限

sentences.en: and the team eventually says no.
sentences.zh: 而这支球队最终拒绝了。

sentences.en: And, when that occurs, that basically means this superstar
sentences.zh: 当这种情况发生时，基本上意味着这位超级巨星

sentences.en: who's been offered many millions of dollars in a variety of different forms
sentences.zh: 曾被以各种不同形式提供数百万美元的报价

sentences.en: ends up being unemployed for the following year.
sentences.zh: 最终在第二年失业了。

sentences.en: So, the agent tells Matthew Harrington that any team that signs him
sentences.zh: 因此，经纪人告诉马修·哈灵顿，任何签下他的球队

sentences.zh: 都必须提供495万美元的第一年签约奖金。

sentences.en: Now, this was an extreme offer at the time.
sentences.zh: 在当时，这是一个极端的报价。

sentences.en: The Colorado Rockies, who chose Harrington as the seventh pick in the draft,
sentences.zh: 科罗拉多落基山队在选秀中以第七顺位选中了哈灵顿，

sentences.en: actually made a number of fairly compelling offers,
sentences.zh: 实际上提出了许多相当诱人的报价，

sentences.en: including $5.3 million over eight years or $3.7 million without a long-term commitment.
sentences.zh: 包括8年530万美元，或者不附带长期承诺的370万美元。

sentences.en: But the agent and the family and the young man declined.
sentences.zh: 但经纪人、家人和这位年轻人拒绝了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, just to put this in perspective, this is in 2000.
sentences.zh: 所以，为了客观地看待这一点，这是在2000年。

sentences.en: So, these dollars are very different than dollars today.
sentences.zh: 因此，这些美元与今天的美元非常不同。

sentences.en: But, still, we were talking about a lot of money being on the table.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管如此，我们谈论的是桌面上有一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And, we were talking about somebody who doesn't have a college education,
sentences.zh: 而且，我们谈论的是一个没有受过大学教育的人，

sentences.en: doesn't have a terrific alternative career outside of baseball,
sentences.zh: 在棒球之外没有出色的替代职业生涯，

sentences.en: who's being offered around $5 million in a variety of different forms,
sentences.zh: 却被以各种不同形式提供大约500万美元的报价，

sentences.en: depending on the number of years that Matt Harrington would sign for.
sentences.zh: 这取决于马修·哈灵顿将签约的年数。

sentences.en: And, Tommy Tanzer, the agent, pushes the Harringtons to be patient and wait for more.
sentences.zh: 经纪人汤米·坦泽则敦促哈灵顿保持耐心，等待更多的报价。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the Colorado Rockies, the baseball team, wants Harrington,
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，科罗拉多落基山队这支棒球队想要哈灵顿，

sentences.en: but not at the price level that Tanzer and Harrington are demanding.
sentences.zh: 但并不愿意接受坦泽和哈灵顿所要求的价格水平。

sentences.en: And, basically, no deal is created.
sentences.zh: 基本上，没有达成任何协议。

sentences.en: So, after holding out this first year, he gets a second shot at the big leagues the following year.
sentences.zh: 因此，在坚持第一年后，他在第二年获得了冲击大联盟的第二次机会。

sentences.en: Matthew Harrington switched agents and entered the Major League Baseball draft again.
sentences.zh: 马修·哈灵顿更换了经纪人，并再次参加了美国职棒大联盟选秀。

sentences.en: This time, the team from San Diego chooses him as the 58th overall selection.
sentences.zh: 这一次，圣地亚哥的球队在总第58顺位选中了他。

sentences.en: But, the final offer they make is $1.25 million over four years with a $300,000 signing bonus.
sentences.zh: 但是，他们最终的报价是4年125万美元，外加30万美元的签约奖金。

sentences.en: Now, that's significantly less than what the Colorado team offered him a year earlier.
sentences.zh: 这比科罗拉多球队前一年给他的报价要少得多。

sentences.en: And, it's also less than what, you know, Tommy Tanzer had promised that he would get
sentences.zh: 而且这也比汤米·坦泽承诺他会得到的要少，

sentences.en: when he became, you know, this baseball star.
sentences.zh: 当他成为这个棒球明星的时候。

sentences.en: So, what happens in year two?
sentences.zh: 那么，第二年发生了什么？

sentences.en: So, we have a very similar kind of phenomena here
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一种非常相似的现象

sentences.en: in terms of Harrington being disappointed that his market value has fallen so dramatically.
sentences.zh: 就哈灵顿对自己的市场价值暴跌感到失望而言。

sentences.en: So, we can easily imagine that there was an anchor set by the prior year,
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以很容易地想象，前一年有一个锚定效应，

sentences.en: and Harrington's hoping for something in the range of what,
sentences.zh: 哈灵顿希望得到的报酬在什么范围内，

sentences.en: at least what he passed on the year before.
sentences.zh: 至少是他前一年放弃的那个水平。

sentences.en: But, during the year, he has not shown his potential, and his value has fallen.
sentences.zh: 但是，在这一年里，他没有展现出自己的潜力，他的价值下降了。

sentences.en: And, basically, with over a million dollars on the table,
sentences.zh: 基本上，在桌上有超过一百万美元的情况下，

sentences.en: and again, this is in year 2000 dollars, or 2001,
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这是2000年或2001年的美元，

sentences.en: he basically passes on the opportunity holding off for more,
sentences.zh: 他基本上放弃了这个机会，等待更多，

sentences.en: and he continues to not be able to pursue playing baseball at the level of the major leagues.
sentences.zh: 并且他继续无法在大联盟级别的水平上打棒球。

sentences.en: And, as a result, his value goes down and down and down over time.
sentences.zh: 结果，随着时间的推移，他的价值一降再降。

sentences.en: And, Harrington never gets the opportunity to be a major league baseball player,
sentences.zh: 哈灵顿再也没有机会成为一名大联盟棒球运动员，

sentences.en: perhaps because Tanzer and Harrington, and then following year, Harrington and his new agent,
sentences.zh: 也许是因为坦泽和哈灵顿，以及第二年的哈灵顿和他的新经纪人，

sentences.en: are basically overconfident that they can obtain an amount that wasn't viable in the first place.
sentences.zh: 他们过于自信，认为自己能获得一个一开始就不可行的金额。

sentences.en: And, certainly, the fact that this happens year after year in the Harrington story
sentences.zh: 当然，在哈灵顿的故事中，这种情况年复一年地发生，

sentences.en: is suggestive of the fact that the Harrington team, with rotating agents,
sentences.zh: 这表明由轮换经纪人组成的哈灵顿团队，

sentences.en: continues to expect more than what the market will provide.
sentences.zh: 继续期望得到超过市场所能提供的金额。

sentences.en: So, I understand that in year three, he comes back to the draft again.
sentences.zh: 所以我听说在第三年，他又回到了选秀中。

sentences.en: This time, he's chosen as the 374th pick by the Tampa Bay team,
sentences.zh: 这一次，他被坦帕湾队在第374顺位选中，

sentences.en: and now he's offered less than $100,000.
sentences.zh: 现在给他的报价不到10万美元。

sentences.en: Now, of course, you know, he'd been previously offered, you know,
sentences.zh: 当然，你知道，他以前曾得到过

sentences.en: three-plus million dollars, and then one-plus million dollars,
sentences.zh: 三百万美元以上，然后是一百万美元以上，

sentences.en: and now $100,000.
sentences.zh: 而现在是10万美元。

sentences.en: And each time, he says, you know,
sentences.zh: 每一次，他都说，

sentences.en: how can I be offered so much less than my value?
sentences.zh: 为什么给我的报价比我的价值低这么多？

sentences.en: He becomes the longest holdout in the history of Major League Baseball.
sentences.zh: 他成为了美国职棒大联盟历史上坚持最久不签约的人。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, the original offer was more in the $5 million range,
sentences.zh: 所以，最初的报价更接近500万美元的范围，

sentences.en: and then a little over $1 million, and then $100,000.
sentences.zh: 然后略高于100万美元，接着是10万美元。

sentences.en: And we can see what's happening.
sentences.zh: 我们可以看到发生了什么。

sentences.en: The market is basically seeing him as a less valuable prospect as the time goes by.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，市场基本上认为他是一个价值较低的潜力新秀。

sentences.en: But, first, he escalates his commitment in year one,
sentences.zh: 但是，首先，他在第一年加大了他的投入承诺，

sentences.en: and then he anchors on prior numbers.
sentences.zh: 然后他锚定于先前的数字。

sentences.en: And he's anchoring on numbers that the market does not see as appropriate
sentences.zh: 他所锚定的数字是市场认为不合适

sentences.en: or even worth paying in order to get him to sign.
sentences.zh: 甚至不值得为了让他签约而支付的数字。

sentences.en: And as a result, he ends up working in a low-level retail context,
sentences.zh: 结果，他最终在底层零售行业工作，

sentences.en: as opposed to ending up as a Major League picture,
sentences.zh: 而不是成为一名大联盟投手。

sentences.en: which seemed to be where his future had been headed.
sentences.zh: 这似乎正是他当时的人生走向。

sentences.en: So, yeah, by the year 2009, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，到了2009年的时候，你知道的，

sentences.en: he's working in the tire department of the local Costco,
sentences.zh: 他在当地的开市客（Costco）轮胎部门工作，

sentences.en: earning $11.50 an hour.
sentences.zh: 时薪是11.50美元。

sentences.en: And, of course, now that decision looks really foolish.
sentences.zh: 当然，现在回过头看，那个决定显得非常愚蠢。

sentences.en: But it's not just the initial contracts that he passed up on.
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是他错过了最初的那些合同。

sentences.en: Presumably, if he had played for these teams and had become a star,
sentences.zh: 据推测，如果他当时为这些球队效力并成为球星，

sentences.en: you know, there would have been future contracts
sentences.zh: 你知道的，未来还会有更多的合同，

sentences.en: that could have also been lucrative.
sentences.zh: 那些合同同样会带来丰厚的回报。

sentences.en: There could have been a future career in coaching and scouting and broadcasting.
sentences.zh: 他未来还可能在教练、球探或广播解说领域发展职业生涯。

sentences.en: There's so many ways in which, you know,
sentences.zh: 有很多迹象表明，你知道的，

sentences.en: his overconfidence at the front end may have cost him a great deal
sentences.zh: 他一开始的过于自信可能会让他付出巨大的代价，

sentences.en: through the rest of his life.
sentences.zh: 甚至影响他的余生。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And he seems to be a very nice human being.
sentences.zh: 而且他似乎是一个非常好的人，

sentences.en: Who copes with these losses well.
sentences.zh: 能够很好地应对这些失落。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 他在体育的其他领域，

sentences.zh: 同样的谈判错误也会出现在我们的个人生活中。

sentences.zh: 婚姻中的每一方都可能会高估自己对这段关系所带来的价值。

sentences.zh: 如果我们问一对恋爱关系中的伴侣，

sentences.en: what percent of the household work do you do?
sentences.zh: 你承担了百分之多少的家务？

sentences.en: Depending on the study, it seems to come in at 120 to 130 percent.
sentences.zh: 根据不同的研究，总和似乎达到了120%到130%。

sentences.en: More recently, Nick Epley and Eugene Caruso and I asked MBA students
sentences.zh: 最近，尼克·埃普利（Nick Epley）、尤金·卡鲁索（Eugene Caruso）和我询问了攻读MBA的学生，

sentences.en: who worked in study groups,
sentences.zh: 他们是在学习小组中工作的，

sentences.en: what percent of the good ideas or what percent of the work came from you?
sentences.zh: 好主意或者工作量里有多少百分比是由你贡献的？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the sum total comes up to more like 140 percent.
sentences.zh: 而总和更接近140%。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: When we ask co-authors of academic papers,
sentences.zh: 当我们询问学术论文的共同作者时，

sentences.en: what percent of the work did you do?
sentences.zh: 你们完成了百分之多少的工作？

sentences.en: We come in at 140 percent
sentences.zh: 结果加起来又是140%，

sentences.en: when the sum total of the actual work has to be 100 percent.
sentences.zh: 而实际工作的总和必须是100%。

sentences.en: And what's going on is we all see the work we did do.
sentences.zh: 出现这种情况的原因是，我们都只看到了自己做过的工作，

sentences.zh: 却不一定能看到其他人所做的工作。

sentences.zh: 所以回想起我的教育经历，我很久以前是个会计专业，

sentences.zh: 这让人觉得我应该有能力自己报税。

sentences.zh: 当我花时间报税时，

sentences.zh: 我的配偶并没有对我的那份工作给予充分的肯定。

sentences.zh: 与此同时，说到遛狗，

sentences.zh: 因为那不是为了狗走的，

sentences.zh: 那是为了玛拉自己走的。

sentences.zh: 存在着极其广泛的偏差。

sentences.zh: 所以，你和尤金·卡鲁索以及尼克·埃普利一起，

sentences.zh: 也研究过一种将注意力从我们自己身上移开，

sentences.en: Tell me about this work, Max.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲这项研究吧，马克斯（Max）。

sentences.en: So let's go back to the context where there's four people working on a project.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们回到这样一个场景：有四个人在一个项目上工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we'll call them A, B, C, and D.
sentences.zh: 我们把他们分别叫做A、B、C和D。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: If we ask each of them, what percent of the work did you do?
sentences.zh: 如果我们问他们每个人：“你完成了百分之多少的工作？”

sentences.en: We get perhaps 140%.
sentences.zh: 我们得到的总和大概是140%。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But if instead we ask A to write down what percent of the work was done by A, B, C, and D,
sentences.zh: 但如果我们转而让A写下A、B、C和D分别完成了百分之多少的工作，

sentences.en: now all of a sudden I as A will think about B, C, and D in a more significant way.
sentences.zh: 现在，作为A的我，就会突然开始以一种更具意义的方式去思考B、C和D的作用。

sentences.en: I'll realize that they, in fact, did do some important work.
sentences.zh: 我会意识到，他们其实确实做了一些很重要的工作。

sentences.en: And that 140% falls.
sentences.zh: 然后那140%的数值就会下降。

sentences.en: So the 140% as the sum total of what each claimed as credit for themselves
sentences.zh: 因此，作为每个人对自己声称的贡献总和的140%，

sentences.en: seems to come down by about half of the overclaiming.
sentences.zh: 似乎会把过度索取的部分减少大约一半。

sentences.en: They're still overclaiming, but it's down to perhaps 120%.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然在过度索取，但已经下降到大约120%了。

sentences.en: In other words, you're focusing now on the contributions of the other people
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你现在把重点放在了其他人的贡献上，

sentences.en: rather than on your own contributions.
sentences.zh: 而不是你自己的贡献上。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: So I'm engaging in less overclaiming, but there's a problem still.
sentences.zh: 所以我减少了过度索取，但仍然存在一个问题。

sentences.en: And the problem is the fact that I'm thinking more about the topic,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，尽管我对这个话题思考得更多了，

sentences.en: I become even more reluctant to deal with these other folks in the future
sentences.zh: 但我未来却变得更加不愿意与这些其他人打交道，

sentences.en: because they didn't do enough work.
sentences.zh: 因为他们没有做够工作。

sentences.en: I'm thinking more about them, and my negative inferences about them go up as a result.
sentences.zh: 我对他们想得更多了，结果我对他们的负面推断也随之增加了。

sentences.en: So we reduce the overclaiming, but we don't create a more constructive group in this process.
sentences.zh: 所以我们减少了过度索取，但在这个过程中我们并没有建立起一个更具建设性的团队。

sentences.en: So one of the problems with overclaiming generally is if the other side doesn't do their fair share of the work,
sentences.zh: 因此，总体而言，过度索取带来的问题之一就是，如果另一方没有完成他们那份公平的工作，

sentences.en: I don't want to work with them in the future.
sentences.zh: 我以后就不想和他们合作了。

sentences.en: So one way to apportion credit properly is to follow the advice of the philosopher John Rawls.
sentences.zh: 所以，合理分配功劳的方法之一就是遵循哲学家约翰·罗尔斯（John Rawls）的建议。

sentences.en: Can you explain what you mean by this, Max?
sentences.zh: 你能解释一下你这是什么意思吗，马克斯？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So John Rawls basically argues if you want to think about what a just society should look like,
sentences.zh: 约翰·罗尔斯基本上认为，如果你想思考一个公正的社会应该是什么样子，

sentences.en: you need to put on a veil of ignorance.
sentences.zh: 你就需要戴上一层面纱，即“无知之幕”。

sentences.en: You need to forget about whether you're male or female.
sentences.zh: 你需要忘掉自己是男是女。

sentences.en: You need to forget about whether you're American or from Lithuania.
sentences.zh: 你需要忘掉自己是美国人还是立陶宛人。

sentences.en: You need to sort of drop all of your own identity to try to imagine how the world should operate
sentences.zh: 你需要抛开你所有的个人身份，去尝试想象世界应该如何运转，

sentences.en: if you didn't know what role you had in society.
sentences.zh: 如果你根本不知道自己在社会中扮演什么角色的话。

sentences.en: And across a number of studies,
sentences.zh: 通过大量的研究，

sentences.en: we find that getting people to try to put on a veil of ignorance allows them to think about what would be just in a much fairer and more objective way.
sentences.zh: 我们发现引导人们戴上“无知之幕”，能让他们以一种更加公平、更加客观的方式去思考什么是公正。

sentences.en: So anytime you're in a dispute,
sentences.zh: 所以，任何当你处于纠纷之中时，

sentences.en: if you could get yourself out of the fact that you're the landlord or you're the tenant
sentences.zh: 如果你能跳出自己是房东还是租客的身份局限，

sentences.en: and think about what a fair resolution would be from the perspective of a third party,
sentences.zh: 并试着从第三方的角度去思考什么是公平的解决方案，

sentences.en: you're more likely to have a bearing on what would be a fair settlement to whatever dispute you happen to be involved in.
sentences.zh: 你就更有可能对你所卷入的任何纠纷找到一个公平的解决办法。

sentences.en: And this idea of using the veil of ignorance comes up across lots and lots of different studies.
sentences.zh: 这种利用“无知之幕”的想法出现在许许多多不同的研究中。

sentences.en: So more recently with Josh Green and others,
sentences.zh: 最近，我们还与乔什·格林（Josh Greene）等人合作，

sentences.en: we even looked at the allocation of scarce resources.
sentences.zh: 研究了稀缺资源的分配问题。

sentences.en: Like you could imagine who gets the limited health resources under COVID.
sentences.zh: 比如你可以想象在新冠疫情期间，谁能获得有限的医疗资源。

sentences.en: And so imagine, for example, there is only one ventilator left
sentences.zh: 试想一下，例如，只剩下一台呼吸机了，

sentences.en: and whoever gets it lives and whoever doesn't get it dies.
sentences.zh: 谁得到它谁就能活下来，谁得不到它就会死去。

sentences.en: And the 65-year-old arrives two minutes before the 25-year-old.
sentences.zh: 而一个65岁的人比一个25岁的人早到了两分钟。

sentences.en: And if we ask the question, who should get it?
sentences.zh: 如果我们提出这个问题：谁该得到它？

sentences.en: We find that people tend to be self-serving in the direction of which of the two people are more like themselves.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们往往倾向于照顾和自己更相似的那个人，带有自私的偏向。

sentences.en: So old people are biased toward the 65-year-old, young people toward the 25-year-old.
sentences.zh: 所以老年人倾向于65岁的人，年轻人则倾向于25岁的人。

sentences.en: But if we encourage people to think about what would be fair if they don't consider their own demographics.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们鼓励人们去思考：如果不考虑各自的人口统计学特征，什么才是公平的？

sentences.en: And now all of a sudden people realize that the 25-year-old has many, many more years to live than the 65-year-old on average.
sentences.zh: 这时候，人们突然意识到，平均而言，25岁的人比65岁的人还有更多、更多的年岁要活。

sentences.en: And now there's a shift among the older people we ask this question to,
sentences.zh: 于是，在我们询问过这个问题的老年人当中，观念发生了转变，

sentences.en: to give this limited resource to where it can do the most good.
sentences.zh: 他们愿意把这有限的资源分配到最能发挥最大价值的地方。

sentences.en: Consistent with what we think Rawls would mean by putting on a veil of ignorance.
sentences.zh: 这与我们认为罗尔斯通过戴上“无知之幕”所要表达的意思是一致的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering in the modern world in which we live, Max,
sentences.zh: 马克斯，我想知道在我们生活的现代世界里，

sentences.en: there are so many ways in which we now collaborate, not just with people face-to-face
sentences.zh: 我们现在有很多协作方式，不仅仅是与面对面、

sentences.en: who are working down the corridor from us, but people who are working remotely,
sentences.zh: 在走廊另一头办公的人合作，还有远程工作的人，

sentences.en: people who are working in other parts of the world.
sentences.zh: 以及在世界其他地方工作的人。

sentences.en: I would imagine that the challenge of apportioning credit fairly,
sentences.zh: 我想象，公平分配功劳的挑战，

sentences.en: of understanding what other people might be contributing,
sentences.zh: 去理解别人可能做出了什么贡献，

sentences.en: of understanding in a negotiation what somebody else is giving,
sentences.zh: 在谈判中去理解别人付出了什么，

sentences.en: becomes so much harder now than it was before.
sentences.zh: 现在变得比以前困难得多了。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And you're highlighting one of the important ways in which the game has changed.
sentences.zh: 你指出了游戏规则发生改变的一个重要方面。

sentences.en: We deal with more people who differ from us today than we ever did before.
sentences.zh: 我们今天打交道的人比以往任何时候都更加与我们不同。

sentences.en: And so we're dealing with people in different locations, from different ethnic groups,
sentences.zh: 因此，我们更加频繁地与来自不同地点、不同族群的人打交道，

sentences.en: on a much, much more regular basis.
sentences.zh: 而且这种频率要高得多得多。

sentences.en: And we're often doing it without seeing them face-to-face.
sentences.zh: 而且我们往往是在不曾面晤的情况下做到这一点的。

sentences.en: So the farther people get, both in terms of our connectivity to them and our identification with them,
sentences.zh: 因此，无论是在我们与他们的联系程度，还是在我们对他们的认同感方面，人们离得越远，

sentences.en: the easier it is to not place full value on what they're bringing to the deal.
sentences.zh: 我们就越容易低估他们在交易中所带来的全部价值。

sentences.en: And how do you fix that?
sentences.zh: 那你如何解决这个问题呢？

sentences.en: Because, of course, I don't know if we're going to go back to a world
sentences.zh: 因为当然了，我不知道我们是否会回到这样一个世界：

sentences.en: where all of the negotiations are always going to be face-to-face.
sentences.zh: 所有的谈判将永远都是面对面进行的。

sentences.en: I mean, we are in a world now where, for better or worse,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们现在生活在一个无论好坏的世界里，

sentences.en: we are stuck with virtual communications and handoffs that can span many, many time zones.
sentences.zh: 我们只能接受虚拟沟通，以及可能跨越许许多多时区的交接工作。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So to begin with, you kind of already brought up an answer.
sentences.zh: 首先，你其实已经提出了一个答案。

sentences.en: To what extent can we put on a veil of ignorance so that we're not as biased by our own lens?
sentences.zh: 我们在多大程度上可以戴上“无知之幕”，从而不那么受自身视角所产生的偏见影响？

sentences.en: We have found that people are pretty good at taking a neutral perspective if we ask them to,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果我们要求人们采取中立的视角，

sentences.en: and to put on a veil of ignorance and think about that problem.
sentences.zh: 并戴上“无知之幕”去思考这个问题，他们其实做得相当不错。

sentences.en: So it's not that we're incapable of thinking about the other side.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是我们没有能力去考虑对方的立场。

sentences.en: We simply don't.
sentences.zh: 我们只是没有去这样做而已。

sentences.en: And the more they're distant from us,
sentences.zh: 而且他们离我们越远，

sentences.en: the easier it is to ignore their critical role in a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 我们就越容易忽视他们在谈判中所起到的关键作用。

sentences.en: So simply stopping and adopting the perspective of the other side
sentences.zh: 因此，只要停下来，站在对方的角度去思考，

sentences.en: not only makes you a nicer person,
sentences.zh: 不仅会让你成为一个更好的人，

sentences.en: but it strategically makes you a more effective person
sentences.zh: 而且从战略上讲，也能让你成为一个更有效率的人，

sentences.en: to understand who they are in the negotiation.
sentences.zh: 从而更好地理解他们在谈判中的身份。

sentences.en: And the failure to consider the perspective of the other side
sentences.zh: 而未能考虑对方的视角，

sentences.en: is one of the key barriers that keeps negotiators from being more effective.
sentences.zh: 正是阻碍谈判人员发挥更高效率的关键障碍之一。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the television show The Office.
sentences.zh: 我想给你放一段电视剧《办公室》（The Office）里的片段。

sentences.en: In this clip, Michael Scott, played by Steve Carell,
sentences.zh: 在这段视频中，由史蒂夫·卡瑞尔（Steve Carell）饰演的迈克尔·斯科特（Michael Scott），

sentences.en: has quit his job as the manager of a paper supply company and started a rival firm.
sentences.zh: 辞去了纸品供应公司经理的工作，并创办了一家竞争对手公司。

sentences.en: Michael and his business partner are now negotiating with the chief financial officer
sentences.zh: 迈克尔和他的商业伙伴正在与他前公司的

sentences.en: of his former company about selling their startup.
sentences.zh: 首席财务官就出售他们的初创公司进行谈判。

sentences.en: Michael, in order to expedite these negotiations,
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，为了加快谈判进程，

sentences.en: we are prepared to make you a very generous offer.
sentences.zh: 我们准备向你提出一份非常慷慨的报价。

sentences.en: And we are prepared to reject that offer.
sentences.zh: 而我们准备拒绝这个报价。

sentences.en: Michael, you haven't even heard that.
sentences.zh: 迈克尔，你甚至都没听听那是什么。

sentences.en: You never accept their first offer.
sentences.zh: 你永远不要接受他们的第一份报价。

sentences.en: What is your second offer?
sentences.zh: 你们的第二份报价是什么？

sentences.en: Are you kidding me?
sentences.zh: 你在开玩笑吗？

sentences.en: That is insultingly low?
sentences.zh: 这也太低了，简直是侮辱人。

sentences.en: I don't even want to hear what your first offer was.
sentences.zh: 我甚至都不想知道你们的第一份报价是多少。

sentences.en: I mean, in some ways, Max, this is comedy, of course,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，从某些方面来说，马克斯，这当然像是个喜剧，

sentences.en: but all of us do this in real life.
sentences.zh: 但我们所有人在现实生活中都会这样做。

sentences.en: We simply don't pay attention to what's important to the other side in a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 我们在谈判中根本不关注对方重视的是什么。

sentences.en: There is something kind of over-the-top obvious about not listening to the other side.
sentences.zh: 不听取对方的诉求，这种做法显然是极其荒谬的。

sentences.en: But so often in real life, we think of negotiations simply as a haggling session
sentences.zh: 但现实中很多时候，我们把谈判单纯看作是一场讨价还价的过程，

sentences.en: when we could be so much more effective if we think about it strategically
sentences.zh: 而如果我们能从战略角度思考，就会高效得多，

sentences.en: by asking, how can I best understand the perspective in which they're making me an offer?
sentences.zh: 我们会问：我怎样才能最好地理解他们向我提出报价时的视角？

sentences.en: To what extent do they need me in their firm?
sentences.zh: 他们在多大程度上需要在公司里有我这个人？

sentences.en: What are they going to do if I don't accept their offer?
sentences.zh: 如果我拒绝他们的报价，他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: This helps me to formulate how far I can push things to my advantage.
sentences.zh: 这有助于我权衡自己能把事情推进到什么程度，从而为我争取利益。

sentences.en: It also provides a basis for understanding where there's interesting opportunities for trades.
sentences.zh: 它也为理解哪些地方存在有趣的交易机会奠定了基础。

sentences.en: I mean, so much of this comes down to how we are anchored in our own minds, Max.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很大程度上取决于我们自身的思维定式，马克斯。

sentences.en: So much of what we've been talking about here comes down to the problem of egocentrism.
sentences.zh: 我们在这里讨论的很多问题，归根结底都是自我中心主义的问题。

sentences.en: We are seeing things from our perspective.
sentences.zh: 我们只从自己的视角看待事物。

sentences.en: We are seeing things from a narrow perspective.
sentences.zh: 我们从一个狭隘的视角看待事物。

sentences.en: We're not able to get out of our own headspace.
sentences.zh: 我们无法跳出自己的思维局限。

sentences.en: We seek confirming evidence to back up what we previously thought.
sentences.zh: 我们寻找确凿的证据来支持我们先入为主的想法。

sentences.en: We don't go out and seek more information from the people we are negotiating with.
sentences.zh: 我们不会主动去向谈判对手了解更多信息。

sentences.en: All of these are ways in which we are trapped inside our own heads.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都是我们作茧自缚的表现。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So sort of a wonderful example of what you just described is the work of Linda Babcock and George Lowenstein.
sentences.zh: 琳达·巴布考克和乔治·洛文斯坦的研究，可以说是你刚才描述的一个绝佳例子。

sentences.en: They basically study people in a legal dispute.
sentences.zh: 他们主要研究陷入法律纠纷中的人们。

sentences.en: So everyone agrees that there's been an accident.
sentences.zh: 大家都承认确实发生了一起事故。

sentences.en: And what they find is that the plaintiff's role, the role representing the injured party,
sentences.zh: 而他们发现，原告方、即代表受害方的一方，

sentences.en: think that the case is worth roughly twice what the party representing the defendant thinks it's worth.
sentences.zh: 认为案件的价值大约是代表被告方的一方所认为的价值的两倍。

sentences.en: And some people say, but it's only a simulation.
sentences.zh: 有些人会说，但这只是一场模拟。

sentences.en: It may only be a simulation.
sentences.zh: 它可能确实只是一场模拟。

sentences.en: But once we put people in those roles, they begin to believe their side has some kind of moral justice to it
sentences.zh: 但一旦我们把人们放到这些角色中，他们就会开始相信自己这一方具有某种程度的道德正义，

sentences.en: that the other side lacks at a remarkable level.
sentences.zh: 而这种正义是对方所缺乏的，达到了惊人的程度。

sentences.en: I understand that over the years, you have fielded many requests for negotiation advice,
sentences.zh: 据我了解，多年来你处理过许多关于谈判建议的请求，

sentences.en: and you regularly receive what you have termed the Sunday night real estate call.
sentences.zh: 并且你经常接到你所谓的周日晚间房地产电话。

sentences.en: What is this call, Max?
sentences.zh: 马克斯，这是一个什么样的电话？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So first of all, why Sunday night?
sentences.zh: 那么首先，为什么是周日晚上？

sentences.en: And the answer is the American institution of the open house in the residential real estate market.
sentences.zh: 答案在于美国住宅房地产市场的开放参观日传统。

sentences.en: So Sunday is the most common day for people to post a time online about when their house will be open
sentences.zh: 因此，周日是人们最常在网上公布房屋开放参观时间的日子，

sentences.en: so you can go take a look at the house without having an appointment, a house, condo, whatever.
sentences.zh: 这样你就可以不用预约直接去看房，不管是房子、公寓还是别的什么。

sentences.en: And as a result, an awful lot of house visitations on the real estate market occur on Sunday.
sentences.zh: 因此，房地产市场上大量的看房活动都发生在周日。

sentences.en: This means that agents are busy on late Sunday afternoon, early evening, as people sometimes decide to make an offer.
sentences.zh: 这意味着由于人们有时会决定出价，经纪人在周日傍晚和夜间初会非常忙碌。

sentences.en: So in an example of the story, I'm at home on Sunday night, and it's 9.30, and my phone rings.
sentences.zh: 所以举个故事中的例子，周日晚上我在家里，当时是9点30分，我的电话响了。

sentences.en: And I pick up the phone and say hi.
sentences.zh: 我接起电话说你好。

sentences.en: And on the other end of the line is somebody who introduces themselves as a friend of a friend of mine.
sentences.zh: 电话那头是一个自称是我朋友的朋友的人。

sentences.en: And I like our mutual friends, so I want to be polite despite the timing of the phone call.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢我们共同的朋友，所以尽管这通电话打得不是时候，我还是想保持礼貌。

sentences.en: And after introducing themselves as a friend of a friend of mine, they explain why they're calling.
sentences.zh: 在自我介绍说是朋友的朋友后，他们说明了打电话的来意。

sentences.en: They looked at a house this afternoon.
sentences.zh: 他们今天下午去看了一套房子。

sentences.en: In fact, they've been looking at houses for the last three months.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们过去三个月一直在看房。

sentences.en: They've looked at over 20 houses.
sentences.zh: 他们看过了20多套房子。

sentences.en: But today they found an amazing house.
sentences.zh: 但今天他们找到了一套令人惊叹的房子。

sentences.en: And they proceed to describe it to me in intricate detail.
sentences.zh: 接着他们开始向我极其详细地描述这套房子。

sentences.en: They seem to be under the illusion that on Sunday night I care what it looks like.
sentences.zh: 他们似乎有一种错觉，觉得周日晚上我在乎它长什么样。

sentences.en: But they proceed to the reason for the call.
sentences.zh: 但他们随后说出了打电话的正事。

sentences.en: So the house is listed for $599,000.
sentences.zh: 这套房子的标价是59万9千美元。

sentences.en: Earlier in the day, at 4.30 in the afternoon, in fact, they made an offer for $550,000.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在当天早些时候的下午4点30分，他们出价55万美元。

sentences.en: So $599,000 offer, asking, and they offered $550,000.
sentences.zh: 所以标价是59万9千美元，而他们出价55万美元。

sentences.en: And that evening they went to our mutual friend's house for dinner.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上他们去了我们共同的朋友家吃晚饭。

sentences.en: And about 10 minutes ago, the agent called back and said that the seller had countered at $585,000.
sentences.zh: 大约10分钟前，经纪人回电话说，卖家还价58万5千美元。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And they want to know what they should do next because they had been talking with their friend who said,
sentences.zh: 他们想知道接下来该怎么办，因为他们和朋友聊过，朋友说：

sentences.en: I know what to do.
sentences.zh: 我知道该怎么办。

sentences.en: Let's call Max.
sentences.zh: 我们给马克斯打电话吧。

sentences.en: He teaches negotiation.
sentences.zh: 他教谈判课。

sentences.en: And when I get this call, and I promise you I've received some version of this call so many times,
sentences.zh: 当我接到这个电话时——我向你保证，这类电话我真的接了无数次——

sentences.en: the first thing I ask them is, what are they going to do if they don't buy this house?
sentences.zh: 我问他们的第一件事是，如果他们不买这套房子，他们会怎么做？

sentences.en: And they typically respond with some notion of, Max, we didn't call you for how not to buy the house.
sentences.zh: 他们的典型反应是某种类似这样的观点：马克斯，我们打电话不是为了听怎么不买这套房子的。

sentences.en: We called you for advice on how to buy the house.
sentences.zh: 我们打电话是向你讨教怎么买下这套房子的建议。

sentences.en: So I've been trying to figure out, what are these people actually asking?
sentences.zh: 所以我一直在琢磨，这些人到底在问什么？

sentences.en: And I think what they're asking is, Max, how do we get a great deal?
sentences.zh: 我想他们的疑问是：马克斯，我们怎样才能拿到一个划算的价格？

sentences.en: And by the way, we don't want to run any risk whatsoever of losing the deal.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们绝不想冒任何失去这笔交易的风险。

sentences.en: And that question I know the answer to is you can't.
sentences.zh: 对于这个问题，我知道答案是：不可能。

sentences.en: To get the best deal possible, you probably need to run some small risk that you'll lose the deal.
sentences.zh: 要想拿到尽可能好的价格，你可能需要冒一点失去交易的小风险。

sentences.en: And if instead of feeling like I have to have this house at any cost, you had a second house or a second and third house that you liked almost as well,
sentences.zh: 如果你不是觉得不惜一切代价也必须买下这套房，而是还有第二套、甚至第二和第三套你同样喜欢的房子，

sentences.en: but you needed to repaint the kitchen, then all of a sudden you're empowered to counter in a way that runs some risk,
sentences.zh: 只不过需要重新粉刷一下厨房，那么突然之间，你就有底气去还价了，虽然这会冒一些风险，

sentences.en: but allows you to get a significantly better price.
sentences.zh: 但能让你谈到一个明显更好的价格。

sentences.en: So if the world ends, if you don't buy this house, you should pay the $5.85.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果不买这套房子就好像世界末日一样，那你应该支付58.5万美元。

sentences.en: If there's another house where buying the other house would make you indifferent between that and paying $5.70,
sentences.zh: 如果有另一套房子，买下它能让你觉得和支付57万美元没有区别，

sentences.en: well, now you can counter at $5.60 knowing no tragedy is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 那么现在你就可以还价56万美元，因为你知道不会发生什么悲剧。

sentences.en: You can always go to the other house instead.
sentences.zh: 你大不了可以去买另一套房子。

sentences.en: So in other words, you say that the most important rule in real estate is to fall in love with three, not with one.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你认为房地产最重要的规则是：爱上三套房子，而不是一套。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And for most negotiations, falling in love with three rather than with one is a pretty good piece of advice.
sentences.zh: 对于大多数谈判来说，爱上三套而不是一套房子，是个相当不错的建议。

sentences.en: When we come back, when to stick to our guns and when to fold.
sentences.zh: 接下来的节目中，我们将讨论什么时候该坚持到底，什么时候该放弃。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedanta.
sentences.zh: 我是香卡·韦丹塔。

sentences.en: We've all seen the movies of cool negotiators who bluff their way into amazing deals.
sentences.zh: 我们都看过电影中那些沉着冷静的谈判专家，他们靠虚张声势谈成了惊人的交易。

sentences.en: By exuding overconfidence and charisma, they get their opponents to fold.
sentences.zh: 他们散发着极度自信和个人魅力，迫使对手妥协。

sentences.en: Real life, of course, is not the movies.
sentences.zh: 当然，现实生活可不是电影。

sentences.en: The people sitting across from you at work or at the kitchen table are unlikely to be overwhelmed by your charisma and overconfidence.
sentences.zh: 坐在你对面工作桌前或餐桌旁的人，不太会被你的个人魅力和极度自信所压倒。

sentences.en: In fact, they've watched the same movies you've watched.
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们也看过你看过的那些电影。

sentences.en: They may also falsely believe that you'll fold if they just push you hard enough.
sentences.zh: 他们也可能错误地认为，只要给你足够的压力，你就会妥协。

sentences.en: Max Bezeman is a social scientist at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 马克斯·巴泽曼是哈佛商学院的一位社会科学家。

sentences.en: He's the author of several books about negotiation, including Negotiating Rationally,
sentences.zh: 他著有多本关于谈判的书籍，包括《理性谈判》、

sentences.en: Negotiation Genius, How to Overcome Obstacles and Achieve Brilliant Results at the Bargaining Table and Beyond,
sentences.zh: 《谈判天才：如何在谈判桌内及桌外克服障碍并取得辉煌成果》，

sentences.en: and, most recently, Negotiation, The Game Has Changed.
sentences.zh: 以及最近出版的《谈判：游戏规则已变》。

sentences.en: Max sometimes advises people who are confronting a negotiation to ask themselves an unusual question.
sentences.zh: 马克斯有时会建议面临谈判的人们问自己一个不同寻常的问题。

sentences.en: How would I feel if the other side instantly accepted my offer?
sentences.zh: 如果对方立刻接受了我的报价，我会有什么感觉？

sentences.en: So I'll tell you a story based on my travels.
sentences.zh: 那我给你讲一个根据我的旅行经历改编的故事。

sentences.en: So I've taught in Thailand a fair amount, and Thailand ends up being kind of a center for sapphires and rubies.
sentences.zh: 我在泰国教过不少时间的书，泰国可以说是蓝宝石和红宝石的中心。

sentences.en: So I'll ask you to imagine that you take a trip to Thailand.
sentences.zh: 所以请你想象一下，你去泰国旅游。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And you're walking down Silom Road, a major market street in town.
sentences.zh: 你走在席隆路上，那是镇上一条主要的商业街。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And for some reason, you know a little bit about sapphires and rubies,
sentences.zh: 不知为何，你对蓝宝石和红宝石略知一二，

sentences.en: and you're walking down the street, and in the window, you see a beautiful ruby ring.
sentences.zh: 当你走在街上时，你在橱窗里看到了一枚漂亮的红宝石戒指。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And your first guesstimate is that it's worth about $5,000.
sentences.zh: 你的初步估算认为它大约值5000美元。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But you don't want to pay anywhere near that because your knowledge is rusty.
sentences.zh: 但因为你的鉴赏知识生疏了，你不想出接近这个数字的高价。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So you go in, you have a conversation with a store owner, and finally you ask to see that ring, and she pulls it out.
sentences.zh: 于是你走进去，与店主交谈，最后你要求看看那枚戒指，她把它拿了出来。

sentences.en: And you ask, how much would this ring cost?
sentences.zh: 你问：这枚戒指要多少钱？

sentences.en: And she says, you know, that ring just showed up yesterday.
sentences.zh: 她说：你知道的，这枚戒指昨天刚到货。

sentences.en: I haven't even put a price on it.
sentences.zh: 我甚至还没给它标价。

sentences.en: But in Thai culture, the first sale of the day brings you luck.
sentences.zh: 但在泰国文化中，一天的第一笔生意能带来好运。

sentences.en: So, Shankar, make me a reasonable offer, and I'll do my best to accept it.
sentences.zh: 所以，香卡，开个合理的价吧，我会尽力接受的。

sentences.en: And you wanting to protect yourself and get a good deal, you pull out $1,000 out of your wallet.
sentences.zh: 为了保护自己并谈成一笔好买卖，你从钱包里掏出了1000美元。

sentences.en: And you say to her, I can give you $1,000, but not a penny more.
sentences.zh: 你对她说：我只能给你1000美元，一分也不能多。

sentences.en: And she says, okay, I'll take it.
sentences.zh: 她说：好的，我接受。

sentences.en: How do you feel?
sentences.zh: 你现在感觉如何？

sentences.en: Well, most people feel unhappy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，大多数人都会觉得很不高兴。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Because her quick acceptance tells them something.
sentences.zh: 因为她这么快接受透露了一些信息。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Like perhaps that isn't a ruby, but rather a red piece of glass.
sentences.zh: 比如那可能根本不是红宝石，而是一块红玻璃。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Now, perhaps before you offer $1,000, it makes sense to think about how would you feel if she accepted it.
sentences.zh: 现在，也许在出价1000美元之前，先想想如果她接受了你会有什么感觉，这是很有意义的。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And this might tell you that I need to have the ring assessed by an independent party before I part with my $1,000.
sentences.zh: 这可能会提醒你，在掏出1000美元之前，我需要找独立第三方对戒指进行评估。

sentences.en: Now, what's intriguing about this is had she haggled with you and allowed you to pay $1,700, you might have been happier.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，如果她跟你讨价还价，让你支付1700美元，你可能会更高兴。

sentences.en: But that wouldn't improve the quality of the glass any more than with the story where you pay $1,000.
sentences.zh: 但这并不会让玻璃的质量比你付1000美元时有所提高。

sentences.en: Now, this may sound remote being about a ring in Thailand, but many of us end up being busy when we take a job in a new city.
sentences.zh: 这听起来可能有点遥远，像是在说泰国的一枚戒指，但我们许多人在新城市找到工作时都会非常忙碌。

sentences.en: And we have limited time to look at the real estate market.
sentences.zh: 我们只有有限的时间去考察房地产市场。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, we fly in and we make what we think is a slightly low offer and the seller says, okay.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们飞过去，给出一个在我们看来略微偏低的报价，而卖家说：好的。

sentences.en: Well, who knew more about the market, the buyer or the seller?
sentences.zh: 那么，谁更了解市场，买家还是卖家？

sentences.en: Yeah, the seller did.
sentences.zh: 嗯，卖家更了解。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And again, this is an example, a different kind of example of what we earlier called the winner's curse.
sentences.zh: 而且再次强调，这是一个例子，是一个不同类型的例子，也就是我们之前所说的“赢者诅咒”。

sentences.en: They're more likely to take your offer when you least want them to.
sentences.zh: 当你们最不希望他们接受时，他们反而更有可能接受你的报价。

sentences.en: So, what I love about the question, will I be happy if my offer is accepted quickly, is that by asking ourselves the question, it's a way of actually pointing out to ourselves,
sentences.zh: 所以，我非常喜欢这个问题——“如果我的报价很快被接受，我会高兴吗？”——是因为通过问自己这个问题，实际上是在提醒我们自己，

sentences.en: we might not know the terrain on which we're standing.
sentences.zh: 我们可能并不了解我们所处的地形。

sentences.en: And therefore, if this offer was accepted quickly, it would actually tell me that, in fact, I do not know the terrain on which I'm standing.
sentences.zh: 因此，如果这个报价很快被接受，实际上就是在告诉我，事实上，我根本不了解我脚下的地形。

sentences.en: I should actually educate myself.
sentences.zh: 我其实应该先做点功课。

sentences.en: And so, the question is really a disguised way of telling me, go out and do more research, go out and learn some more.
sentences.zh: 所以，这个问题实际上是一种委婉的说法，提醒我去外面做更多的调研，去多学习一点。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And when we think about things more deliberatively in advance of negotiation, we prepare more thoroughly and we're more effective in negotiation.
sentences.zh: 当我们如果在谈判前进行更多深思熟虑的思考，我们就会准备得更充分，在谈判中也会更有效率。

sentences.en: Max says that he is often surprised by how little research people do before going into a negotiation.
sentences.zh: 马克斯说，他经常对人们在谈判前做那么一点点调研感到惊讶。

sentences.en: One of the aspects of the modern world is that there's so much information online.
sentences.zh: 现代社会的一个特点就是网上有太多丰富的信息。

sentences.en: And this means that we can so often do our homework to have a better idea of what the zone of possible agreement might look like before the negotiation ever begins.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我们在谈判开始之前，就能经常做好功课，对可能达成协议的区间有一个更好的概念。

sentences.en: So, one of my favorite examples is the negotiation context that so many people find terrifying, which is going and buying a new car.
sentences.zh: 所以，我最喜欢的例子之一就是许多人感到恐惧的谈判场景，那就是去买一辆新车。

sentences.en: And what I find fascinating about the fact that people are terrified by this task is that it's so easy to get good information about the dealer cost of a car online.
sentences.zh: 让我觉得有趣的是，人们竟然会害怕这项任务，因为在网上获取汽车经销商成本的好信息实在是太容易了。

sentences.en: There's probably better than a dozen websites that will allow you to punch in the details of what you want to buy and find out the dealer coSt.
sentences.zh: 大概有十几个以上的网站可以让你输入你想买的汽车的详细信息，并查出经销商的成本。

sentences.en: And once you do that, it allows you to have a very good idea of what the zone of possible agreement should look like.
sentences.zh: 一旦你这样做了，它就能让你对可能达成协议的区间有一个很好的概念。

sentences.en: And going back to your question, if you're going to put the number on the table, you want to put a number that's favorable to you,
sentences.zh: 回到你的问题，如果你要把这个数字摆在桌面上，你想给出一个对你有利的数字，

sentences.en: but yet reasonable enough that you're not so far worse than the other sides that they end up walking without wanting to talk to you anymore.
sentences.zh: 但同时又要足够合理，不至于比对方差得太远，以至于他们最后拂袖而去，再也不想和你谈下去。

sentences.en: I want to go back to Bangkok, Thailand for a second.
sentences.zh: 我想稍微回到泰国曼谷去。

sentences.en: As you mentioned, Max, you used to teach the art of negotiation to students there.
sentences.zh: 正如你所提到的，马克斯，你过去常在那里教学生谈判的艺术。

sentences.en: But I understand that your students would challenge you on your own negotiation skills when it came to hiring taxicabs?
sentences.zh: 但我听说，在雇出租车时，你的学生会挑战你自己的谈判技巧？

sentences.en: So, every morning, class started the same way.
sentences.zh: 所以，每天早上，课堂都是以同样的方式开始的。

sentences.en: I was teaching a group of Thai students and I was teaching negotiation.
sentences.zh: 我当时正在教一群泰国学生，我教的是谈判。

sentences.en: Of course, they want to know, does this professor actually know anything in the real world?
sentences.zh: 当然，他们想知道，这位教授在现实世界里到底懂不懂什么？

sentences.en: And their favorite way of assessing this is to say, professor, where did you go last night?
sentences.zh: 而他们最喜欢的评估方式就是问：教授，你昨晚去哪儿了？

sentences.en: And after I would tell them, they would say, and how much did you pay the taxi driver to bring you home?
sentences.zh: 在我告诉他们之后，他们会说：那你付了多少车费让出租车司机把你送回家的？

sentences.en: Now, I need to put this into perspective.
sentences.zh: 现在，我需要把这放在当时的背景下来看。

sentences.en: So, this is before the taxi system changed in Bangkok to using meters.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是曼谷的出租车系统改用计价器之前的事。

sentences.en: And before taxis used meters, you basically haggled with the taxi driver.
sentences.zh: 在出租车使用计价器之前，你基本上要和出租车司机讨价还价。

sentences.en: You'd tell them where you want to go and they would make me an offer, which would be too high, and you'd haggle.
sentences.zh: 你会告诉他们你想去哪里，然后他们会给你出一个价，这个价会开得很高，然后你就得讨价还价。

sentences.en: And typically, in about 40 seconds, you'd converge on a price.
sentences.zh: 通常在大约40秒内，你们就会就一个价格达成一致。

sentences.en: You know, the first few days, they laughed at me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，前几天，他们都在笑话我。

sentences.en: And they would basically tell me that I paid 40 cents too much or 80 cents too much.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上会告诉我，我多付了40美分或者80美分。

sentences.en: And that gave them a great chuckle and they were happy.
sentences.zh: 这让他们觉得非常好笑，他们也很高兴。

sentences.en: But I would say within two weeks, I had some increased credibility based on my sort of mastering the art of negotiating with the taxi driver.
sentences.zh: 但我想说，不到两周时间，由于我掌握了与出租车司机讨价还价的艺术，我建立了一些信誉。

sentences.en: But then the problem showed up, and that was my spouse.
sentences.zh: 但随后问题就出现了，那就是我的配偶。

sentences.en: She flies into town.
sentences.zh: 她飞到了这座城市。

sentences.en: We go for a long walk the first evening to go to a restaurant across town, come out of the restaurant.
sentences.zh: 第一天晚上，我们去散了长长的步，去城另一头的一家餐馆，从餐馆出来。

sentences.en: And my wife, Marla, she's a bit tired from having flown from the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我的妻子玛拉，因为那天从美国飞到曼谷，觉得有点累了。

sentences.en: to Bangkok that day.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I held down a taxi.
sentences.zh: 我拦下了一辆出租车。

sentences.en: And in my best tie, I say to the taxi driver,
sentences.zh: 我用我最好的泰语对出租车司机说，

sentences.en: which I think means something like, can you take me to the Shell station by the corner of Jaranpan?
sentences.zh: 我想这大概是说：你能把我送到查兰潘（Jaranpan）路口附近的壳牌加油站吗？

sentences.en: And in response to this, he holds up seven fingers for 70 baht,
sentences.zh: 作为回应，他伸出了七根手指，代表70泰铢，

sentences.en: which is basically worth $2.80 at the time of the story.
sentences.zh: 在故事发生的时候，这基本上相当于2.80美元。

sentences.en: A dramatically high price for the ride I was asking him about.
sentences.zh: 对于我向他询问的那段车程来说，这是一个高得离谱的价格。

sentences.en: So I respond by holding up three fingers or $1.20.
sentences.zh: 所以我伸出三根手指作为回应，也就是1.20美元。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: To which he responds with five fingers or $2.
sentences.zh: 对此，他伸出了五根手指，也就是2美元作为回应。

sentences.en: Eventually, he comes down to four fingers or $1.60.
sentences.zh: 最后，他降到了四根手指，也就是1.60美元。

sentences.en: I'm holding at $1.20, which I've already taken this ride for $1.20,
sentences.zh: 我坚持1.20美元，因为我已经以1.20美元的价格坐过这趟车了，

sentences.en: so I know I can get it for $1.20.
sentences.zh: 所以我知道我可以用1.20美元拿下它。

sentences.en: And he responds by driving away.
sentences.zh: 而他的回应是开车走人。

sentences.en: So I held down another taxi driver who starts at a much more reasonable five fingers or $2.
sentences.zh: 所以我又拦下了另一位出租车司机，他一开始给出的价格要合理得多，是五根手指或2美元。

sentences.en: I respond $1.20.
sentences.zh: 我回应1.20美元。

sentences.en: He comes down to four fingers or $1.60.
sentences.zh: 他降到了四根手指或1.60美元。

sentences.en: And I respond with three fingers and he drives away.
sentences.zh: 我伸出三根手指回应，然后他开车走了。

sentences.en: At which point, Marla, my tired spouse, says, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 就在这时，我疲惫的配偶玛拉说：这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: And I explained to her that they were both asking for $1.60 when the fare price is $1.20.
sentences.zh: 我向她解释说，他们俩都要价1.60美元，而实际的车费应该是1.20美元。

sentences.en: And she says, so you're telling me I'm standing here because you're too cheap to pay an extra $0.40?
sentences.zh: 她说：所以你是说，我站在这里，只是因为你太抠门，不愿多付40美分？

sentences.en: And I said, well, you have to understand.
sentences.zh: 我说：嗯，你得理解。

sentences.en: I have to explain to my students tomorrow morning how much I paid.
sentences.zh: 我明天早上得向我的学生们解释我付了多少钱。

sentences.en: And this did not impress my spouse at all.
sentences.zh: 而这并没有给我妻子留下任何好印象。

sentences.en: And so in this story, you have this notion of sort of is it worth the cost of disputing?
sentences.zh: 所以在这个故事中，你有了这样一种概念，也就是争论的成本是否值得？

sentences.en: So I was literally keeping my tired spouse awake on the streets of Bangkok, Thailand over $0.40.
sentences.zh: 所以我居然为了40美分，字面意义上让疲惫的妻子在泰国曼谷的街头熬夜。

sentences.en: And you can easily argue that I could have paid the additional $0.40.
sentences.zh: 你完全可以说，我本可以多付那40美分。

sentences.en: So you can see how getting a good deal can take over things.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以看到，为了占到便宜是怎么让事情失控的。

sentences.en: But it is such a powerful story because I think it shows how negotiations, I think, have a way of sucking us in.
sentences.zh: 但这真是一个很有力的故事，因为我认为它展示了谈判如何有一种把我们卷入其中的方式。

sentences.en: And then we're almost enmeshed in the narrative of the negotiation that we lose track of the bigger picture.
sentences.zh: 然后我们几乎深陷于谈判的叙事中，以至于我们忘记了更大的全局。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And to this day, I'm still guilty of when I'm looking for a hotel online or an airfare online.
sentences.zh: 直到今天，每当我在网上找酒店或机票时，我依然会犯这种毛病。

sentences.en: I over-search to the point where I'm working for a wage that I wouldn't remotely accept if someone offered me work at that wage.
sentences.zh: 我过度搜索，甚至到了这种地步：如果有人按这个工资雇我工作，我是绝对不会接受的，但我却在为这个工资付出劳动。

sentences.en: So this notion of getting a good deal can become obsessive in ways that don't make a whole lot of sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，这种追求占便宜的想法可能会变得强迫性，达到完全没有道理的地步。

sentences.en: In our companion story to this episode, available exclusively to subscribers to Hidden Brain Plus,
sentences.zh: 在我们这期节目的配套故事中，该故事仅向“隐藏的大脑加号”（Hidden Brain Plus）订阅者开放，

sentences.en: we explore what Max calls integrative bargaining, negotiating in a way that tries to leave both parties better off.
sentences.zh: 我们探讨了马克斯所说的“综合性谈判”，即试图让双方都变得更好的谈判方式。

sentences.en: Max says a crucial idea in getting to win-win outcomes is to negotiate multiple issues at the same time
sentences.zh: 马克斯说，实现双赢结果的一个关键理念是同时谈判多个议题，

sentences.en: instead of going after them one at a time, as many of us are prone to do.
sentences.zh: 而不是像我们许多人习惯的那样，一个接一个地去谈。

sentences.en: As soon as we have two or more issues in a negotiation, the parties are likely to have different valuations on those issues.
sentences.zh: 一旦我们在谈判中有两个或更多的议题，双方对这些议题的估价很可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: And if we can find out who cares more about which issue, we can make wise trades that create value and make both of us better off.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能找出谁更在意哪个议题，我们就能做出明智的交易，从而创造价值，让双方都变得更好。

sentences.en: We also examined the single biggest psychological obstacle to coming up with win-win outcomes.
sentences.zh: 我们还探讨了实现双赢结果的最大心理障碍。

sentences.en: It has to do with a certain mindset that is extremely common.
sentences.zh: 这与某种极其常见的思维模式有关。

sentences.en: Max says fixing this one error can save companies and litigants lots of money and save relationships much grief and heartache.
sentences.zh: 马克斯说，纠正这一个错误可以为公司和诉讼当事人省下大笔金钱，并为各方人际关系免去许多痛苦和悲伤。

sentences.zh: 本期《我无名无姓的英雄》由“探索发现”信用卡赞助播出。

sentences.en: Our story comes from Paul Cotter.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事来自保罗·科特。

sentences.en: More than 40 years ago, when Paul's father was in his early 50s, he began to show signs of early-onset Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.zh: 40多年前，当保罗的父亲刚满50岁时，他开始出现早发性阿尔茨海默病的迹象。

sentences.en: But no one suspected cognitive decline, and his father lost job after job.
sentences.zh: 但当时没有人怀疑是认知能力下降，他的父亲一份接一份地失去了工作。

sentences.en: He was no longer able to make decisions, and he couldn't handle the slightest amount of pressure.
sentences.zh: 他再也无法做出决定，也承受不起哪怕一丝一毫的压力。

sentences.en: Since there was no medical explanation given for what he was going through,
sentences.zh: 由于当时对他的遭遇没有任何医学解释，

sentences.en: everyone assumed he was having a crisis of confidence,
sentences.zh: 大家都以为他只是遭遇了自信危机，

sentences.en: and he was told that he needed to pull himself together.
sentences.zh: 并被告知他需要振作起来。

sentences.en: My father, as you can imagine, felt totally humiliated.
sentences.zh: 正如你可以想象的那样，我父亲感到极其羞辱。

sentences.en: After he was diagnosed with Alzheimer's, he was horrified by the news,
sentences.zh: 在他被诊断出患有阿尔茨海默病后，他对这个消息感到震惊，

sentences.en: but I imagine he also felt some sense of relief.
sentences.zh: 但我想他也感到了一些解脱。

sentences.en: Finally, there was an explanation for his decline.
sentences.zh: 终于，他的病情衰退有了解释。

sentences.en: And in spite of it all, he still wanted to keep working.
sentences.zh: 尽管经历了这一切，他仍然想继续工作。

sentences.en: And this is where My Unsung Hero stepped in.
sentences.zh: 而这就是我的“无名英雄”介入的时候。

sentences.en: It wasn't a single person, but a whole company.
sentences.zh: 这不是某一个人，而是一家公司。

sentences.en: A small firm located in our hometown in Buffalo offered my father a job,
sentences.zh: 我们家乡布法罗的一家小公司为我父亲提供了一份工作，

sentences.en: knowing full well that he was suffering from Alzheimer's disease.
sentences.zh: 他们很清楚他患有阿尔茨海默病。

sentences.en: They hired my father to handle small tasks, like making copies.
sentences.zh: 他们雇用我父亲处理一些小任务，比如复印。

sentences.en: They gave him a paycheck, which made him feel needed and valued.
sentences.zh: 他们给他发薪水，这让他觉得自己是被需要和有价值的。

sentences.en: But more than just a job, they gave him respect, dignity, and a sense of purpose
sentences.zh: 但不仅仅是一份工作，他们在他人生分崩离析之际，

sentences.en: at a time when his life was falling apart.
sentences.zh: 给予了他尊重、尊严和目标感。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, my father's disease ultimately progressed to the point
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，我父亲的病情最终恶化到这样的地步：

sentences.en: where he was having problems keeping his balance.
sentences.zh: 他甚至连保持平衡都成了问题。

sentences.en: One day at work, he fell off a small stepladder.
sentences.zh: 有一天在工作时，他从一个小A字梯上摔了下来。

sentences.en: He wasn't hurt, but it was clear to everyone
sentences.zh: 他没有受伤，但每个人都很清楚，

sentences.en: that it was no longer safe for him to continue working.
sentences.zh: 他继续工作已经不再安全了。

sentences.en: The company told my father and my mother in a very compassionate way
sentences.zh: 这家公司以一种非常富有同情心的方式向我父亲和母亲表示，

sentences.en: that it was with deep regret that they'd have to let him go.
sentences.zh: 他们怀着深深的遗憾不得不让他离职。

sentences.en: On my father's final day on the job,
sentences.zh: 在我父亲在岗的最后一天，

sentences.en: they threw him a party to thank him for his service.
sentences.zh: 他们为他举办了一个派对，感谢他所做出的贡献。

sentences.en: What a beautiful, remarkable gesture that was.
sentences.zh: 那是多么美好、多么卓越的举动啊。

sentences.en: I wish my brothers, my sister, and I could remember the name of this company.
sentences.zh: 我真希望我的兄弟姐妹和我能记住这家公司的名字。

sentences.en: Forty years later, we don't know if they're still in business
sentences.zh: 40年后，我们不知道他们是否还在营业，

sentences.en: or what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 或者他们后来怎么样了。

sentences.en: If I could see them today, I would tell them,
sentences.zh: 如果我今天能见到他们，我会对他们说：

sentences.en: thank you from the bottom of my heart.
sentences.zh: 发自内心地感谢你们。

sentences.en: Your kindness during my father's final chapter will never be forgotten.
sentences.zh: 在我父亲人生的最后篇章中，你们的善良永远不会被忘记。

sentences.zh: 并向那些在社区中展现这种精神的人致敬。
